claim: Four builds of one action RPG with none, medium, high and extreme juice: both extremes reduced play time, experience, intrinsic motivation and performance; medium and high scored best.
title: The Effects of Juiciness in an Action RPG

claim: Feedback contingent on player success raised curiosity, competence and effectance, while raw amplification of feedback reduced them, in a pre-registered study of about 1,700 players.
title: How does Juicy Game Feedback Motivate? Testing Curiosity, Competence, and Effectance

claim: Visual embellishments raised aesthetic appeal but had no effect on usability or performance across three games including one built from plain cubes.
title: Juicy Game Design

claim: Players calibrating eight hit-feedback parameters showed individual optima spanning a wide range in three clusters, judged random settings excessive about 45 percent of the time, and camera-shake time correlated with hit stop.
title: Quantifying Hit Feedback Preferences in 2D Action Games: A User-Adjustment Study of Visual and Temporal Parameters

claim: Of nineteen impact-feedback features compared across well and poorly rated action games, hit stop, sound coherence and camera control dominate perceived impact.
title: What Features Influence Impact Feel? A Study of Impact Feedback in Action Games

claim: Adding audio to a visual-only game interface raised immersion, confidence and satisfaction without a performance gain.
title: Multi-sensory Game Interface Improves Player Satisfaction but not Performance

claim: Isolated items are remembered better even when presented before any context, so distinctiveness against a homogeneous background, not perceptual salience, drives the effect.
title: The subtlety of distinctiveness: What von Restorff really did

claim: Juicing is amplification that communicates the importance of game events, and the survey frames proportionality as its function.
title: Designing Game Feel: A Survey

claim: Animacy ratings for a single moving dot rose with the magnitude of speed change and direction change.
title: Perception of Animacy from the Motion of a Single Object

claim: In isomorphic game variants differing by one feature, removing the goal or the uncertain outcome cost more preference than any other single removal.
title: Toward a Theory of Intrinsically Motivating Instruction

claim: Enjoyment of the challenge predicted overall enjoyment across four difficulty rounds where objective difficulty alone did not.
title: Being enjoyably challenged is the key to an enjoyable gaming experience: an experimental approach in a first-person shooter game

claim: Levels are generated two-tiered: rhythm groups of beats and pauses first, then geometry fitted to the rhythm, with pacing parameters on top.
title: Launchpad: A Rhythm-Based Level Generator for 2-D Platformers

claim: Step charting splits into placement (when, conditioned on difficulty) and selection (which), and placement is a rest-dominated class-imbalanced problem.
title: Dance Dance Convolution

claim: Per-event chart generators fail to reproduce human patterning, the congruent relations between placed objects that raters treat as authored.
title: TaikoNation: Patterning-focused Chart Generation for Rhythm Action Games

claim: Plotting generated levels on metrics such as linearity and leniency exposes generator bias and unreachable regions of the design space.
title: Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator

claim: In a social deduction board game, deceptive statements were about twice as likely to contain a silent pause and those pauses were longer, while pitch showed no reliable association.
title: Speech timing cues reveal deceptive speech in social deduction board games

claim: Across 206 documents and about 24,000 judges, lie detection accuracy averaged 54 percent, with truths judged more accurately than lies.
title: Accuracy of Deception Judgments

claim: Chess masters' recall advantage vanishes on randomly arranged boards, so expertise is chunking of recurring legal configurations.
title: Perception in chess

claim: Perceptual learning yields discovery effects, extracting the relevant relation, and fluency effects, extracting it faster, and abstract perceptual learning transfers to novel instances.
title: Perceptual learning and human expertise

claim: From spectator accounts of StarCraft the authors derive personas and a theory of information asymmetry as the source of suspense, implying value in controlling how and when information is uncovered.
title: Starcraft from the Stands: Understanding the Game Spectator
